humanoid.description: An upright biped. Axes run -1 to 1 with 0 neutral, unless noted. Every combination of these values is guaranteed to produce a valid body; a reader that clamps out-of-range values to the stated bounds will always be able to build one.

height.description: Standing height in millimetres. Extreme builds may exceed this slightly, since a body that cannot be constructed is worse than one a little off its nominal stature. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

shoulderWidth.description: Width of the shoulder girdle. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

hipWidth.description: Width of the pelvis. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

limbLength.description: Limb length relative to the torso. Longer limbs raise the pelvis and so shorten the torso at a fixed stature. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

neckLength.description: Neck length. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

headSize.description: Head size. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

headBreadth.description: How broad the skull is across, at a fixed head size: negative is a narrow head, positive a broad one. It scales the head's lateral half-extent only, so a broad skull is broad from the parietal down through the angle of the jaw while staying exactly as deep and as tall. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

faceLength.description: How long the face is below the eyes, at a fixed head size: negative is a short face, positive a long one. It moves the head's joint up its own neck, so what changes is how much of the skull sits below it - the jaw, the chin and the whole feature stack - while the cranium above is untouched. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

extremitySize.description: Hand and foot size. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestVolume.description: How much chest there is, over what femininity, mass, bodyFat and age already predict (#273). An offset on the derived chest and not a slider of its own: zero is whatever the composites came to, so a record keeps meaning what it meant when the formulas improve. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestProjection.description: How far the chest stands off the ribcage against how far it spreads across it, at a fixed volume: negative spreads it, positive stands it off. The shape axis rather than the size one, the same separation headSize and faceLength exist to make. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestLift.description: How high the chest sits, over what age and bodyFat predict: positive lifts it and refuses the descent ageing asks for, negative lets it hang. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestSpacing.description: How far apart the pair sits, over the azimuth the shape derives: negative is close-set, positive wide. An angle about the trunk's own axis rather than a lateral offset, so the separation a body delivers does not depend on how far its chest stands off. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

chestFullness.description: Where the volume sits between the upper pole and the lower one, over the split the shape derives: positive is a fuller lower pole, negative an evenly divided one, at a fixed volume and projection. Not a second ptosis axis - ageing descends the peak toward a fold that holds still, while this moves the split and the fold under it together. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

quadruped.description: A four-legged creature. Axes run -1 to 1 with 0 neutral, unless noted.

height.description: Height of the back line in millimetres. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

bodyLength.description: Body length from shoulder to hip. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

build.description: Overall mass, from slight to heavy. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

muscle.description: Musculature. Thousandths, 0 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

legLength.description: Legginess. Longer legs slim the body at a fixed back height. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

neckLength.description: Neck length. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

headSize.description: Head size. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

tailLength.description: Tail length. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

composites.description: The high-level description of a body: axes named for something about a person rather than about a body part, each fanning out through formulas to many quantities at once. The per-region axes on an archetype apply as offsets on top of what these derive. Kept beside the archetype rather than inside it because the body, the skull and the skin all read them. Shape axes are thousandths as elsewhere; bodyFat is thousandths of a fraction and age is whole years, not thousandths.

femininity.description: Where the body sits between the masculine and feminine references: -1000 fully masculine, +1000 fully feminine, 0 the midpoint of the two. Read by the frame, the fat distribution and the skull together, so a body cannot disagree with itself about it.

mass.description: How much body there is, from slight to heavy. Thousandths, -3000 to 3000. Sets the girth budget; bodyFat decides how it is spent and where. A heavier body carries it in the fleshy sites and barely at all in the bony ones.

bodyFat.description: What share of the body is fat, in thousandths of a fraction: 30 is about the essential fat of a very lean athlete and 600 is past where a silhouette keeps changing. Not stretched past its ends the way a shape axis is, because a negative fraction is not a leaner person but an absence of one.

age.description: How old the body is, in WHOLE YEARS rather than thousandths. Adults only: child proportions are a different envelope and a separate decision, not the bottom of this slider.

skin.description: A body's complexion. Axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type. Every combination is a usable complexion.

melanin.description: Base depth of tone, from palest to deepest. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

undertone.description: Hue beneath the tone: -1000 cool and pink, +1000 warm and olive.

blush.description: How much blood shows through at cheeks, ears, and knuckles. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

eyes.description: How a body's eyes are shaped and set. Axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type. Eyes are geometry that moves rather than a painted feature, so these place a globe and the lids that close over it.

size.description: Eye size, as a fraction of the head's radius. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

spacing.description: How far apart the eyes are set: -1000 close, +1000 wide. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

depth.description: How deeply the eyes are set: -1000 protruding, +1000 sunken. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

aperture.description: How far open the lids rest: 0 shut, 1000 wide. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

inner.description: The iris beside the pupil, in sRGB. Two colours with a gradient between them, the way hair fades from roots to tips: this one at the pupil's edge, 'outer' at the periphery. Three channels, thousandths. Free rather than a point on a pigment ramp, so fantasy eyes need no special case.

outer.description: The iris at its periphery, in sRGB, faded to from 'inner' across the disc. Three channels, thousandths.

ring.description: The limbal ring around the iris, in sRGB — the circle that makes an iris read as an iris rather than a coloured disc. Three channels, thousandths.

outfit.description: What a body is wearing. Close-fitting garments are cut from the body's own surface a few millimetres outside it, so they fit any wearer without being re-cut and cannot intersect the body. Colour axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type.

sleeve.description: How far down the arm the top's sleeves run. Named for where the hem lands, not for a tailoring term: a cut follows the body's zones and an arm carries two of them, so 'forearm' ends about 70% of the way down and 'wrist' at 93%. Readers that do not recognise a value should fall back to 'forearm'.

leg.description: How far down the leg the trousers run. As with the sleeve, named for where the hem lands: the middle cut finishes below the knee rather than at it. Readers that do not recognise a value should fall back to 'ankle'.

topHue.description: The top's colour around the wheel. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

topShade.description: How light the top is. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

legHue.description: The trousers' colour around the wheel. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

legShade.description: How light the trousers are. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

face.description: How prominent a body's facial features are, and how wide. Placed from the published proportion canons - the face divides into thirds from hairline to brow to the base of the nose to the chin, and into fifths across, one fifth being an eye's width - so the prominence axes say how far each feature stands out, not where it sits, and the width axes say how far it reaches across. The skull's own breadth and the face's length are not here: they are properties of the body plan, since they are built into the body rather than carved into it. Thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type.

nose.description: How far the nose stands out: 0 flat, 1000 prominent. Thousandths. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

noseWidth.description: How wide the nose is across the wings: 0 narrow, 1000 broad. Independent of how far it stands out. Thousandths. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

brow.description: How heavy the brow ridge is. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

mouth.description: How full the lips are. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

mouthWidth.description: How wide the mouth is, corner to corner. Independent of how full the lips are. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

ears.description: How far the ears stand out from the head. Thousandths, -1000 to 2000. Exploration envelope (#160): readers clamp to these bounds and every combination still builds.

hairCut.description: How one region of hair is cut. Thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type.

length.description: How far the hair runs past the region it grows from. 0 is cropped to the skin.

thickness.description: How wide each element of hair is. Width costs nothing to draw, so this is the axis a reader should reach for before density.

density.description: How many elements are grown, as a share of what the region can hold. A reader may draw fewer for distant or low-end rendering, which does not change the record.

droop.description: How far the hair gives up its own body and falls with the ground. 0 stands off the skin, 1000 lies flat on it.

hairPaint.description: Hair painted into the skin's own colour, under whatever is grown on top of it. It is what stops thin hair reading as none, and it is the whole of a region a record asks for without geometry: a shaved jaw, a drawn-on brow.

density.description: How much of the skin it covers. Density rather than opacity: at 1000 the skin under the mask is that colour, and between the two the grain shows through, which is what stubble is.

colour.description: What colour, in sRGB. Three channels, thousandths.

scalpRegion.description: Where hair may grow on the scalp: the hairline, and how it recedes.

line.description: Where the hairline sits. -1000 receding, +1000 low on the brow. The whole curve moves together.

temples.description: How deeply the hairline notches back at the temples. 0 is square across the brow and 1000 is two deep bays. Separate from the line because recession is not a raised hairline: a hairline that moved up as a whole is a high forehead, and one that kept its midline peak while the corners went back is what the word recession means.

nape.description: Where the hair stops at the back. -1000 shaved high up the nape, +1000 low onto the neck.

browRegion.description: Where the eyebrows sit. These say where the brow IS, which both layers obey, rather than what is grown on it: changing a haircut does not move a brow ridge.

rise.description: How high the brow sits over the eye. -1000 low and heavy, +1000 high.

apart.description: How far apart the two are. -1000 nearly meeting, +1000 well parted.

reach.description: How far the tail runs past the eye's outer corner. -1000 short, +1000 long.

arch.description: How much the brow arches. -1000 a straight bar, +1000 a high curve. Zero is the arch an ordinary brow has, not a flat one.

moustacheRegion.description: Where hair may grow on the upper lip.

width.description: How far past the mouth's corners it grows. -1000 narrow, +1000 wide.

drop.description: How far down toward the vermilion it grows. -1000 shy of it, +1000 onto its border.

chinRegion.description: Where hair may grow on the chin and the plane under it.

width.description: How wide the patch is. -1000 a narrow tuft, +1000 the whole chin.

under.description: How far under the jaw it reaches. -1000 the chin's front only, +1000 well back along the submental plane.

rise.description: How far up toward the lower lip it grows. -1000 low on the chin, +1000 to the lip's own border.

flankRegion.description: Where hair may grow on the flanks of the jaw, from the sideburn down over the jawline.

cheek.description: How high up the cheek it grows. -1000 a low beard line, +1000 high on the cheekbone.

under.description: How far below the jawline it rides. -1000 stopping on the border, +1000 well down the neck.

sideburn.description: How far forward of the ear the sideburn begins. -1000 well back, +1000 onto the cheek.

follicleRegions.description: Where each of the five kinds of hair may grow on one head. Shape rather than style: these move where hair MAY be, which both layers obey, and say nothing about what is grown there. A hairline is a property of a head and stays where it is when somebody changes their haircut.

scalpStyle.description: The hair of the head. One name, plus whatever axis that style carries; a style with no axis of its own carries none.

name.description: Which style. Readers that do not recognise a value should draw nothing rather than substitute another style: a haircut nobody chose is worse than none.

fringe.description: BOB only: how much shorter the front is than the sides. 0 an even curtain, 1000 a fringe well above the brow.

weight.description: LONG only: how much longer the back is than the sides. 0 even all round, 1000 strongly back-weighted.

tail.description: TIED_BACK only: where the tail is gathered. 0 at the nape, 1000 high on the crown.

curl.description: CURLY only: how tight the coil is. 0 a loose wave, 1000 a tight curl.

browStyle.description: The eyebrows. Most faces should have one drawn even where none is grown: a bare brow ridge reads as a mannequin from across a room.

name.description: Which style. Readers that do not recognise a value should draw nothing rather than substitute another style: a haircut nobody chose is worse than none.
Which style. Readers that do not recognise a value should draw nothing rather than substitute another style: a haircut nobody chose is worse than none.

sweep.description: HANDLEBAR only: how far the ends sweep past the mouth's corners. 0 barely past them, 1000 a full waxed curl.

ride.description: PENCIL only: how high the line sits. 0 on the lip's own border, 1000 halfway to the nostrils.

name.description: Which style. Readers that do not recognise a value should draw nothing rather than substitute another style: a haircut nobody chose is worse than none.

point.description: GOATEE only: how the hang ends. 0 a rounded tuft, 1000 drawn to a point.

twist.description: BRAIDED only: how tightly the rope turns. 0 a loose rope, 1000 a hard twist.

name.description: Which style. Readers that do not recognise a value should draw nothing rather than substitute another style: a haircut nobody chose is worse than none.

drop.description: SIDEBURNS only: how far down the strip runs. 0 a tab beside the ear, 1000 down to the jaw's corner.

reach.description: FULL_CONNECT only: how far below the jawline the beard rides. 0 stopping on the crease, 1000 down onto the upper neck.

scalpTress.description: The hair of the head, both layers.

style.description: Which base style is grown here, and its own axis if it has one. A style of 'none' grows no geometry, which is how a record asks for a region that is painted and not grown.

roots.description: The colour at the roots, in sRGB. Free rather than a point on a pigment ramp, so that grey and dyed hair need no special case.

tips.description: The colour at the tips, likewise, faded to along each element as a vertex colour.

skin.description: The hair painted into the skin under this region.

tips.description: The colour at the tips, likewise, faded to along each element as a vertex colour.

hair.description: The hair on a body's head: five follicle regions, each drawn in two layers over one shared mask — hair painted into the skin, and low-poly geometry grown on top of it. Absent means the default, which is a cropped head with full brows and no facial hair. Both layers read the same mask, so a reader that draws only the painted layer still puts hair where the record says it is.

regions.description: Where each kind of hair may grow, which both layers obey.
